# fairfax

> Open source CLI and cited dataset that checks a Microsoft US government cloud plan (GCC, GCC High, DoD, Azure Government) against Microsoft's own feature availability tables. 633 features across Azure, Power Platform and Microsoft 365, 8 cross-cloud rules, 57 endpoint mappings and 9 cross-cloud sign-in errors; every entry quotes the Microsoft row it came from and carries the page's updated date and the date it was last checked.

- Install: `pip install fairfax` (Python 3.10+, MIT, one dependency: PyYAML). Version 0.2.1.
- `fairfax check plan.yaml`: findings grouped as blocked, cross-cloud, retiring, notes and ok, with Microsoft 365 roadmap items on blocked features; exits 1 when anything is blocked. Text, Markdown, JSON or SARIF.
- `fairfax scan <path> --tenant gcchigh --azure government`: finds commercial hosts in code (login.microsoftonline.com, graph.microsoft.com, *.vault.azure.net, api.security.microsoft.com) and names the government host.
- `fairfax explain AADSTS900439 --tenant gcchigh`: decodes a cross-cloud sign-in error from the code or the whole message: Microsoft's wording, the cause and the right sign-in host.
- `fairfax facts --grep <text>`: feature keys and their status per cloud. `--format json` for data.
- `fairfax verify`: re-reads every cited Microsoft page and confirms each cited row is still there.
- `fairfax mcp`: Model Context Protocol server (stdio) with find_features, check_plan, scan_code and explain_error tools. `claude mcp add fairfax -- fairfax mcp`.
- GitHub Action: `uses: intikhab49/fairfax@v0.2.1` with `plan` and `scan` inputs; job summary, line annotations, optional SARIF upload to code scanning.
- It works offline (except verify). It never connects to a tenant or subscription, and it is not compliance advice.
- Independent project by Intikhab Azam, not affiliated with Microsoft.

## Availability tables

- [Microsoft Sentinel in Azure Government, GCC, GCC High and DoD](https://intikhab49.github.io/fairfax/availability/sentinel/): Which Microsoft Sentinel features work in Azure Government, and which Microsoft 365 connectors work for GCC, GCC High and DoD. 54 entries, each cited.
- [Microsoft Defender for Cloud in Azure Government](https://intikhab49.github.io/fairfax/availability/defender-for-cloud/): Which Defender for Cloud plans and features are available in Azure Government versus commercial Azure. 24 features from Microsoft's tables, each cited.
- [Azure Machine Learning in Azure Government](https://intikhab49.github.io/fairfax/availability/azure-machine-learning/): Which Azure Machine Learning features work in Azure Government versus commercial Azure, with region limits. 23 features, each cited.
- [Azure OpenAI models in Azure Government](https://intikhab49.github.io/fairfax/availability/azure-openai/): Which Azure OpenAI models Microsoft sells in Azure Government and their deployment types in usgovarizona and usgovvirginia. 11 models, each cited.
- [Azure AI Language in Azure Government](https://intikhab49.github.io/fairfax/availability/azure-ai-language/): Which Azure AI Language features have a US Gov Virginia or US Gov Arizona region, and which one is retiring. 5 features, each cited.
- [Power Platform in GCC, GCC High and DoD](https://intikhab49.github.io/fairfax/availability/power-platform/): Which Power Apps, Power Automate, Copilot Studio, Power Pages, AI Builder and Dataverse features work in GCC, GCC High and DoD. 70 features, each cited.
- [Microsoft 365 Copilot in GCC, GCC High and DoD](https://intikhab49.github.io/fairfax/availability/microsoft-365-copilot/): Which Microsoft 365 Copilot features work in GCC, GCC High and DoD: Researcher, Create, agents, Copilot in Teams and more. 25 features, each cited.
- [Microsoft Teams in GCC, GCC High and DoD](https://intikhab49.github.io/fairfax/availability/teams/): Which Teams features and app capabilities work in GCC, GCC High and DoD: shared channels, webinars, third-party apps, workflows. 35 features, each cited.
- [Exchange Online in GCC, GCC High and DoD](https://intikhab49.github.io/fairfax/availability/exchange-online/): Which Exchange Online features work in GCC, GCC High and DoD, with Microsoft's key considerations for each. 90 features, each cited.
- [SharePoint and OneDrive in GCC, GCC High and DoD](https://intikhab49.github.io/fairfax/availability/sharepoint-onedrive/): SharePoint and OneDrive features Microsoft says are missing or limited in GCC, GCC High and DoD, quoted sentence by sentence. 13 features, each cited.
- [Microsoft Purview in GCC, GCC High and DoD](https://intikhab49.github.io/fairfax/availability/purview/): Status of Microsoft Purview features in GCC, GCC High and DoD (available, in development, on the engineering backlog) from Microsoft's three planning pages. 230 features.
- [Microsoft Intune in GCC High and DoD](https://intikhab49.github.io/fairfax/availability/intune/): Which Intune features Microsoft lists as not available or planned for GCC High and DoD, such as Windows Autopilot and Remediations. 35 features, each cited.
- [Defender for Endpoint and Defender XDR in GCC, GCC High and DoD](https://intikhab49.github.io/fairfax/availability/defender/): Feature parity of Defender for Endpoint, Defender XDR and Defender Vulnerability Management in GCC, GCC High and DoD, from Microsoft's tables. 18 features, each cited.
- [Overview and sources](https://intikhab49.github.io/fairfax/availability/): every service, every cited Microsoft page, download links
- [Endpoints](https://intikhab49.github.io/fairfax/endpoints/): 57 commercial-to-government host mappings

## Sign-in errors

- [AADSTS50049 NoSuchInstanceForDiscovery](https://intikhab49.github.io/fairfax/errors/aadsts50049/): The authority your app was given isn't a known Microsoft Entra instance, often a typo in the sign-in host or a host from the wrong cloud.
- [AADSTS90002 InvalidTenantName](https://intikhab49.github.io/fairfax/errors/aadsts90002/): Microsoft Entra ID can't find the tenant on the host you asked. Microsoft says this often happens because a cross-cloud app was used…
- [AADSTS90038 NationalCloudTenantRedirection](https://intikhab49.github.io/fairfax/errors/aadsts90038/): The tenant you're signing in to belongs to a different national cloud from the sign-in host you used, and the two clouds don't federate.…
- [AADSTS90051 InvalidNationalCloudId](https://intikhab49.github.io/fairfax/errors/aadsts90051/): The national cloud identifier in the request isn't valid, for example a misspelled or mixed-up cloud name in your authentication library's…
- [AADSTS700016 UnauthorizedClient_DoesNotMatchRequest](https://intikhab49.github.io/fairfax/errors/aadsts700016/): The app wasn't found in the tenant. In US government setups a common cause is an app registered in one cloud (for example Azure…
- [AADSTS900382 Confidential Client isn't supported in Cross Cloud request](https://intikhab49.github.io/fairfax/errors/aadsts900382/): Same message as AADSTS900432: a confidential client (an app with a secret or certificate) asked for a token across clouds, and Microsoft…
- [AADSTS900432 Confidential Client isn't supported in Cross Cloud request](https://intikhab49.github.io/fairfax/errors/aadsts900432/): An app that signs in with a secret or certificate (a confidential client) asked for a token across clouds, for example an app registered…
- [AADSTS900439 USGClientNotSupportedOnPublicEndpoint](https://intikhab49.github.io/fairfax/errors/aadsts900439/): Your app signed in a GCC High, DoD or Azure Government user through the commercial sign-in host, login.microsoftonline.com. Microsoft…
- [AADSTS1000104 XCB2BResourceCloudNotAllowedOnIdentityTenant](https://intikhab49.github.io/fairfax/errors/aadsts1000104/): A user from one cloud tried to reach a resource in another cloud (cross-cloud B2B), and the tenant's settings don't allow that pairing of…

## Exchange Online in GCC, GCC High and DoD

- Exchange Online: Hybrid deployment supported (`exchange/hybrid-deployment-supported`). GCC: Available; GCC High: Available; DoD: Available. For coexistence with Exchange Server on-premises, Microsoft requires installing at least one Exchange Server 2013 Client Access Server (or Exchange Server 2016.). Exchange Server 2010 and earlier aren't supported. Source: Exchange Online for US government environments, page updated 2025-12-02: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office365/servicedescriptions/office-365-platform-service-description/office-365-us-government/exchange-online-for-us-government-environments#exchange-online-features . Microsoft's row: Hybrid deployment supported | Yes | Yes | Yes
- Exchange Online: IMAP migration supported (`exchange/imap-migration-supported`). GCC: Available; GCC High: Available; DoD: Available. Source: Exchange Online for US government environments, page updated 2025-12-02: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office365/servicedescriptions/office-365-platform-service-description/office-365-us-government/exchange-online-for-us-government-environments#exchange-online-features . Microsoft's row: IMAP migration supported | Yes | Yes | Yes
- Exchange Online: Cutover migration supported (`exchange/cutover-migration-supported`). GCC: Available; GCC High: Available; DoD: Available. Source: Exchange Online for US government environments, page updated 2025-12-02: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office365/servicedescriptions/office-365-platform-service-description/office-365-us-government/exchange-online-for-us-government-environments#exchange-online-features . Microsoft's row: Cutover migration supported | Yes | Yes | Yes
- Exchange Online: Staged migration supported (`exchange/staged-migration-supported`). GCC: Available; GCC High: Available; DoD: Available. GSuite migration isn't supported for GCC High and DoD. ## Cross-cloud rules

- GCC signs in through commercial Entra ID: Office 365 GCC signs users in through commercial Entra ID: login.microsoftonline.com, graph.microsoft.com and portal.azure.com, the same endpoints as worldwide Microsoft 365. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/fundamentals/feature-availability#microsoft-365-integration (high)
- GCC High and DoD sign in through Azure Government: GCC High and DoD sign users in through Entra ID in Azure Government: login.microsoftonline.us, with graph.microsoft.us (GCC High) or dod-graph.microsoft.us (DoD). Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/fundamentals/feature-availability#microsoft-365-integration (high)
- Tenant and Azure subscription are in different clouds: Your Microsoft 365 tenant lives in commercial Entra ID, but your Azure subscription is in Azure Government. A token from one cloud is rejected by the other, so every call across that line needs an app registration and credentials in the cloud being called. A managed identity in Azure Government can't sign in to your GCC tenant. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/deployments#microsoft-graph-and-graph-explorer-service-root-endpoints (high)
- Tenant and Azure subscription are in different clouds: Your Microsoft 365 tenant lives in Entra ID in Azure Government, but your Azure subscription is in commercial Azure. A token from one cloud is rejected by the other, so every call across that line needs an app registration and credentials in the cloud being called. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/deployments#microsoft-graph-and-graph-explorer-service-root-endpoints (high)
- GCC support has no location or citizenship assurances: GCC support runs on worldwide terms: Microsoft gives no assurances about where support agents are or what citizenship they hold. Background checks apply only to staff who can reach customer content. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office365/servicedescriptions/office-365-platform-service-description/office-365-us-government/gcc#office-365-government-gcc-customer-support (high)
- Power Platform calls into commercial Azure cross clouds: Power Platform for GCC and GCC High runs in Azure Government, so calls from your flows and apps to commercial Azure services cross clouds. If a service sits behind a firewall (Azure SQL, for example), the firewall must allow the Azure Government IP ranges for AzureCloud.usgovtexas and AzureCloud.usgovvirginia. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/powerapps-us-government#connectivity-between-power-apps-us-government-and-public-azure-cloud-services (high)
- Azure Machine Learning in Azure Government needs its own firewall hosts: Azure Machine Learning in Azure Government needs usgovvirginia.api.ml.azure.us or usgovarizona.api.ml.azure.us open in your firewall, depending on the region. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/machine-learning/reference-machine-learning-cloud-parity?view=azureml-api-2#other-azure-government-limitations (high)
- Entra ID logs from a GCC tenant into Sentinel in Azure Government: Your tenant's Entra ID is in commercial Azure, and your Sentinel workspace is in Azure Government. Microsoft's tables list the Entra ID connector in both clouds, but none covers sending a commercial tenant's sign-in logs to an Azure Government workspace. Test it before you depend on it. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/fundamentals/feature-availability#microsoft-purview-data-connectors (unverified)

- Microsoft Defender XDR API: Commercial Azure: api.security.microsoft.com, us.api.security.microsoft.com, eu.api.security.microsoft.com, uk.api.security.microsoft.com, au.api.security.microsoft.com, swa.api.security.microsoft.com, ina.api.security.microsoft.com, aea.api.security.microsoft.com; GCC: api-gcc.security.microsoft.us; GCC High: api-gov.security.microsoft.us; DoD: api-gov.security.microsoft.us. ## Cross-cloud sign-in errors

- AADSTS50049 NoSuchInstanceForDiscovery: The authority your app was given isn't a known Microsoft Entra instance, often a typo in the sign-in host or a host from the wrong cloud. Fix: Use the sign-in host for your tenant's cloud exactly as Microsoft lists it. Microsoft: "AADSTS50049 | NoSuchInstanceForDiscovery - Unknown or invalid instance." Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/reference-error-codes#aadsts-error-codes (medium)
- AADSTS90002 InvalidTenantName: Microsoft Entra ID can't find the tenant on the host you asked. Microsoft says this often happens because a cross-cloud app was used against the wrong cloud: a GCC High, DoD or Azure Government tenant doesn't exist on login.microsoftonline.com. Fix: Check the tenant ID, then sign in through the host of the cloud that tenant lives in. Microsoft: "AADSTS90002 | InvalidTenantName - The tenant name wasn't found in the data store. Check to make sure you have the correct tenant ID. The application developer will receive this error if their app attempts to sign into a tenant that we cannot find. Often, this is because a cross-cloud app was used against the wrong cloud, or the developer attempted to sign in to a tenant derived from an email address, but the domain isn't registered." Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/reference-error-codes#aadsts-error-codes (high)
- AADSTS90038 NationalCloudTenantRedirection: The tenant you're signing in to belongs to a different national cloud from the sign-in host you used, and the two clouds don't federate. Typical cause: a GCC High, DoD or Azure Government tenant reached through login.microsoftonline.com, or the other way round. Fix: Send the request to the sign-in host of the tenant's own cloud. Microsoft: "AADSTS90038 | NationalCloudTenantRedirection - The specified tenant 'Y' belongs to the National Cloud 'X'. Current cloud instance 'Z' does not federate with X. A cloud redirect error is returned." Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/reference-error-codes#aadsts-error-codes (high)
- AADSTS90051 InvalidNationalCloudId: The national cloud identifier in the request isn't valid, for example a misspelled or mixed-up cloud name in your authentication library's settings. Fix: Check the cloud or instance setting your library uses against the endpoint for your tenant's cloud. Microsoft: "AADSTS90051 | InvalidNationalCloudId - The national cloud identifier contains an invalid cloud identifier." Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/reference-error-codes#aadsts-error-codes (medium)
- AADSTS700016 UnauthorizedClient_DoesNotMatchRequest: The app wasn't found in the tenant. In US government setups a common cause is an app registered in one cloud (for example Azure Government) while the token request goes to the other cloud's sign-in host, where the app doesn't exist. Fix: Check which cloud the app registration lives in and send the request to that cloud's sign-in host, with that tenant's ID. Microsoft: "AADSTS700016 | UnauthorizedClient_DoesNotMatchRequest - The application wasn't found in the directory/tenant. This can happen if the application has not been installed by the administrator of the tenant or consented to by any user in the tenant. You might have misconfigured the identifier value for the application or sent your authentication request to the wrong tenant." Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/reference-error-codes#aadsts-error-codes (medium)
- AADSTS900382 Confidential Client isn't supported in Cross Cloud request: Same message as AADSTS900432: a confidential client (an app with a secret or certificate) asked for a token across clouds, and Microsoft doesn't support that. Fix: Register the app in the same cloud as the tenant it calls, and request tokens from that cloud's sign-in host. Microsoft: "AADSTS900382 | Confidential Client isn't supported in Cross Cloud request." Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/reference-error-codes#aadsts-error-codes (high)
- AADSTS900432 Confidential Client isn't supported in Cross Cloud request: An app that signs in with a secret or certificate (a confidential client) asked for a token across clouds, for example an app registered in commercial Entra ID calling into a GCC High tenant. Microsoft doesn't support confidential clients in cross-cloud requests. Fix: Register the app in the same cloud as the tenant it calls, and request tokens from that cloud's sign-in host. Microsoft: "AADSTS900432 | Confidential Client isn't supported in Cross Cloud request." Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/reference-error-codes#aadsts-error-codes (high)
- AADSTS900439 USGClientNotSupportedOnPublicEndpoint: Your app signed in a GCC High, DoD or Azure Government user through the commercial sign-in host, login.microsoftonline.com. Microsoft Entra ID has blocked that since 2020: users in US Government tenants must sign in through login.microsoftonline.us. Fix: Point the app's authority at login.microsoftonline.us. If the app is registered in a commercial tenant and is meant to serve US Government users, Microsoft says it may need a new app registration in the US Government cloud. Microsoft: "Impacted apps will begin seeing an error AADSTS900439 - USGClientNotSupportedOnPublicEndpoint. This error indicates that the app is attempting to sign in a US Government user on the public cloud endpoint." Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/reference-breaking-changes#azure-government-endpoints-are-changing (high)
- AADSTS1000104 XCB2BResourceCloudNotAllowedOnIdentityTenant: A user from one cloud tried to reach a resource in another cloud (cross-cloud B2B), and the tenant's settings don't allow that pairing of clouds. Fix: Either allow B2B collaboration with the other Microsoft cloud in the tenant's cross-tenant access settings, or use an account from the resource's own cloud. Microsoft: "AADSTS1000104 | XCB2BResourceCloudNotAllowedOnIdentityTenant - Resource cloud {resourceCloud} isn't allowed on identity tenant {identityTenant}. {resourceCloud} - cloud instance which owns the resource. {identityTenant} - is the tenant where signing-in identity is originated from." Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/reference-error-codes#aadsts-error-codes (medium)
